steps.u: TokenBucketLimiter has zero tests. Write a proper unit test class for it.

steps.a: It takes an injectable `LongSupplier` clock, so I can drive time deterministically. One thing stands out: `(elapsedMs / 1000)` is integer division, so any call less than a second after the previous one adds zero tokens, and because `lastNanos` is still reset, frequent callers never refill. I'll write the tests and pin that case down with a test that fails today, disabled so the suite stays green, rather than changing the limiter, since you only asked for tests.

steps.a: Added TokenBucketLimiterTest with a fake clock: 3 passing tests (drain, refill after 1s, capacity cap) and 1 @Disabled test that reproduces a real bug: `refill()` uses integer division on elapsed seconds and resets `lastNanos`, so callers more often than once a second never get tokens back. Confirmed it fails when enabled. The fix is to compute `elapsedNanos / 1e9 * refillPerSecond` as a double; I haven't changed the limiter.

reference.summary: Wrote a JUnit 5 test class for a Java token bucket rate limiter using an injected fake clock. While writing it, found a refill bug where integer division on elapsed seconds plus resetting the last refill time means frequent callers never refill, and captured it in a disabled failing test instead of fixing the code. The 3 enabled tests pass, and the disabled test was confirmed to fail.
